overview: This Senate resolution honors the victims and survivors of the August 27, 2025, mass shooting at Annunciation Catholic Church and School in Minneapolis, Minnesota, where a shooter opened fire during a back-to-school Mass, killing two children and injuring 21 others. The resolution condemns the attack, offers condolences to the families, and praises police, medical teams, school and church staff, and community members who responded. It declares that everyone deserves to feel safe in schools and places of worship and expresses solidarity with other communities affected by gun violence. It does not change any law or spending. The Senate approved it by unanimous consent on September 8, 2025.
for: Supporters say the Senate speaking with one voice offers comfort to a grieving community and recognizes the bravery of those who helped during the attack.
against: Critics say the resolution is symbolic: it doesn't change any law or provide new resources to prevent similar attacks.
